name: iPhone
description: The iPhone (1st generation), announced in 2007, was Apple's first smartphone and marked the company's entry into the mobile phone market. it introduced a multi-touch interface and combined the functions of a mobile phone, iPod, and internet device

specs.sensors: Accelerometer, Proximity sensor, Ambient light sensor

hardware: The original iPhone was powered by a Samsung S5L8900 processor based on the ARM11 architecture, running at approximately 412 MHz, and included 128MB of RAM. it was sold in 4GB, 8GB and later 16GB storage configurations. the device contained a 1400 mAh lithium-ion battery and included sensors such as an accelerometer, proximity sensor, and ambient light sensor. it supported GSM cellular networks but did not include 3G capability.
software: At launch, the iPhone ran iPhone OS 1, which featured applications such as Safari, Mail, Photos, Maps, YouTube, and iPod. The operating system used a touch-based interface with gestures like pinch-to-zoom. Native third-party applications were not supported initially; Apple instead promoted web applications accessed through the browser. The App Store was introduced in 2008 with iPhone OS 2, and the device was eventually upgradable to iPhone OS 3.1.3.
connectivity: the iPhone suppported quad-band GSM and EDGE (2G) data networks, along with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 2.0. it did not include 3G cellular data, GPS or MMS messaging at launch. internet access was provided through the Safari browser, which rendered full desktop-style web pages rather than simplified mobile versions.
camera: The device included a single 2-megapixel rear camera designed for still photography. it did not support video recording, autofocus, flash or a front facing camera. images could be viewed and managed through the Photos application and synchronised with a computer using iTunes.
release_and_reception: the iPhone was unveiled by Steve Jobs at Macworld 2007 and released later that year in the united states through an exclusive carrier agreement with AT&T. it initially retailed at $499 and $599 with a two-year contract, depending on storage capacity. early reviews praised its touchscreen interface, web browsing experience, and designm while criticism focused on the lack of 3G connectivity, limited customisation, and absence of thrid-party apps at launch
impact/legacy: the original iPhone is widely regarded as one of the most influential consumer electronics devices of the 21st century. it helped popularise capacitive touchscreens, app-based software ecosystems, and the use of full web browsers on mobile phones. its design approach - prioritising a large touchscreen and minimal physical controls - became the dominant model for modern smartphones.
design: The original iPhone introduced a design that felt years ahead of its time. it featured a sleek aluminum back paired with a black plastic section at the bottom to allow radio signals to pass through - a necessary compromise that still looked intentional and premium. the front was dominated by a 3.5-inch display, something usually large for phones in 2007, and was almost entirely free of buttons, apart from a single circular home button. its curved edges, slim profile, and minimalist layout reflected Apple's philosophy of simplicity and elegance. the absence that would define smartphones for years to come

name: iPhone 3G
description: The iPhone 3G, released on July 11, 2008, was the second generation of Apple's smartphone and the first to include 3G cellular connectivity. it retained manny design elements of the original iPhone but introduced faster data transfer, GPS support, and the launch of the App Store, enabling third-party native applications for the first time. The device continued Apple's focus on touchscreen-based interaction, combining phone, iPod, and internet functionality

specs.sensors: Accelerometer, Proximity sensor, Ambient light sensor, GPS

hardware: The iPhone 3G used the same Samsung S5L8900 ARM11 processor at 412 MHz as the original iPhone, with 128 MB of RAM. storage options included 8 GB and 16 GB. it contained a 1150 mAh lithium-ion battery, slightly smaller than the original, due to improved efficiency in 3G networks. the device added GPS support and included the same sensors as the original iPhone: accelerometer, proximity sensor, and ambient light sensor, it supported 3G HSDPA networks for faster mobile internet access.
software: The iPhone 3G launched with iPhone OS 2, introducing the App Store, which allowed users to download and install thrid-party native applications. it included built-in applications such as Safari, Mail, Maps, iPod, and YouTube. the operating system retained the multi-touch interface and gesture controls while adding enterprise features such as Microsoft Exchange support, it was later upgradeable to iPhone OS 4.2.1.
connectivity: The iPhone 3G supported quad-band GSM and tri-band 3G networks, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth 2.0. It included GPS for location services, enabling turn-by-turn navigation and location-based applications. The device continued to lack video calling and relied on the Safari browser for full internet access.
camera: The rear camera remained a single 2-megapixel unit without video recording, autofocus, or flash. Photos could be viewed on the device or synchronised with a computer using iTunes. The iPhone 3G did not include a front-facing camera.
release_and_reception: Apple announced the iPhone 3G at the Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) on June 9, 2008, and released it on July 11, 2008, in 22 countries. Prices ranaged from $199 for the 8 GB model to $299 for the 16 GB model with a 2-year carrier contract. Reviews praised the faster 3G connectivity, GPS functionality, and App Store integration, though battery life under 3G usage was sometimes criticised. The device was seen as a major step in the iPhone lineup's evolution.
impact/legacy: The iPhone 3G cemented Apple's role in the smartphone industry by introducing native apps via the App Store and modern location-based services. its 3G connectivity and GPS capabilities set the standard for future smartphones and expanded the functionality beyond multimedia and communication to include navigation and mobile productivity.
design: The iPhone 3G featured a more rounded plastic back comared to the aluminum and plastic combination of the original iPhone, which improved signal reception for the new 3G capabilities. The front remained dominated by the 3.5-inch display with a single Home button below it. it measured 115.5 x 62.1 x 12.3 mm and weighed 133 grams, making it slightly thicker and lighter than its precedessor. physical controls included a sleep/wake button on top, volume buttons and mute switch on the left, and a recessed 3.5 mm headphone jack on top. The device was available in black and, later, white.

name: iPhone 3GS
description: The iPhone 3GS, announced on June 8, 2009, and released on June 19, 2009, was the third-generation iPhone. building on the iPhone 3G, it offered improved performance, a higher-quality camera, video recording, and voice control. the 'S' stood for 'Speed', highlighting the device's faster processor and enhanced responsiveness. The iPhone 3GS retained the touchscreen-based interface and multi-function design combining phone, iPod and internet capabilities.

specs.sensors: Accelerometer, Proximity sensor, ambient light sensor, and digital compass

hardware: The iPhone 3GS introduced a faster 600 MHz Samsung ARM Cortex-A8 processor and doubled RAM to 256 MB. Storage options included 8GB, 16GB, and 32GB. a 1219 mAh lithium-ion battery provided power, supporting longer usage despite the increased performance. The device featured a 3-megapixel rear camera capable of 640 x 480 video recording at 30 fps, autofocus, and basic image stabilisation. Sensors included an accelerometer, proximity sensor, ambient light sensor, and digital compass. 3G HSDPA conenctivity and GPS were retained.
software: The iPhone 3GS launched with iPhone OS 3, introducing features such as copy and paste, video recording, and voice control. The App Store continued to expand, allowing users to download third-party apps. Later iOS updates brought additional functionalities, including multitasking and home screen folders. The device was ultimately upgradeable to iOS 6.1.6.
connectivity: The iPhone 3GS supported quad-band GSM, tri-band 3G HSDPA networks, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 2.1. GPS functionality enabled location-based services, navigation, and geotagging photos. internet access was available via Safari or third-party apps, and cellular performance was significantly improved over the iPhone 3G.
camera: The rear camera was upgraded to 3 megapixels, added autofocus, and introduced video recording at 30 frames per second. it retained no front-facing camera. Photos could be geotagged using GPS data, and videos could be viewed and managed on the device or synced through iTunes.
release_and_reception: The iPhone 3GS was unveiled at WWDC 2009 and released on June 19, 2009. Prices at launch were $199 for the 16 GB model and $299 for the 32 GB model with a 2-year contract. The device was praised for its improved speed, enhanced camera, and new software features, though some reviewers noted that the design remained largely unchanged from the 3G.
impact/legacy: The iPhone 2GS strengthened Apple's dominance in the smartphone market by combining hardware improvements with software enhancements. features such as video recording, voice control, and a faster processor set new expectations for mobile devices. it laid the groundwork for future iPhones that focused on performance, camera quality, and richer multimedia experiences.
design: The iPhone 3GS maintained the rounded plastic back and overall form factor of the iPhone 3G, measuring 115.5 x 62.1 x 12.3 mm and weighing 135 grams. the front featured the same 3.5-inch display with a Home button below it. Minor design refinements included improved material finish for scratch resistance. Physical buttons and ports remained unchanged, including the sleep/wake button on top, volume buttons and mute switch on the left, recessed 3.5 mm headphone jack, and 30-pin dock connector. The device was available in black and white.
